mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY growth falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening in monetary and price stability policy, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive divergence between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS growth) for three consecutive months signals a buildup of household savings, which typically precedes a delayed but sustained consumption rebound and positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > RSAFS growth for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth exceeds RSAFS growth for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the unemployment rate to below 3.5% while payroll employment growth remains robust signals a tight labor market that boosts wage pressures and inflation expectations, which ultimately erodes corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE falls below 3.5% and PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.3% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.
